## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The containment check in `preview` must be fixed before merge: it compares paths lexically, so a `..` segment or a symlink reads files outside the home directory. The added outside-path test covers only an absolute path, so it does not catch this.

## Changes
Adds `preview(home, relative)`, which returns the first 200 characters of a file under `home`, and `settings_file(home)`, which returns the `settings.toml` path, to `app/paths.py`, with tests for both. It also adds `tests/review-note.txt`, which no test reads.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — Resolve the candidate before the home containment check — `preview(home, "../outside.txt")` returns the first 200 characters of a file outside `home` instead of raising `ValueError`. `Path.is_relative_to` compares components lexically, so `home/../outside.txt` counts as inside `home`; a symlink under `home` that points outside passes the same way. — A caller that passes a user-supplied relative path exposes the start of any file the process can read. — Fix: Compare `(Path(home) / relative).resolve()` against `Path(home).resolve()`, and extend `test_preview` with a `..` case and a symlink case.

## Important
- app/paths.py:14 — correctness — Decode previews with an explicit encoding and error handler — `preview(home, "photo.png")` on a UTF-8 locale raises `UnicodeDecodeError` instead of returning a preview. `read_text()` decodes strictly with the locale's default encoding, and `UnicodeDecodeError` subclasses `ValueError`, the type line 13 raises for outside-home paths. — A caller catching `ValueError` cannot tell an undecodable file inside home from a rejected outside path.

## Suggestions
- app/paths.py:14 — correctness — Read only the first 200 characters, not the whole file — `preview` on a multi-gigabyte log under `home` loads and decodes the entire file to return 200 characters, because `candidate.read_text()[:200]` slices after the full read. — Previewing one large file costs memory and time proportional to its size.
